description: An introduction to soil, its formation, components, profile, types, physical properties, fertility, pH and importance to crop growth.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best describes soil?

options.text: The solid rock layer found deep underground
The thin upper layer of the earth where plants grow
A mixture of only water and air
Decayed leaves piled on a forest floor

mcq.explanation: Soil is the thin natural top layer of the earth's surface in which plants are able to grow.

mcq.questionText: The breaking down of rocks into smaller particles to form soil is called:
mcq.explanation: Weathering is the process by which rocks are broken down into smaller particles that eventually form soil.

mcq.questionText: Which type of weathering is caused by the action of living organisms such as plant roots and burrowing animals?
mcq.explanation: Biological weathering is the breakdown of rocks by living organisms such as roots, earthworms and microorganisms.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is NOT one of the main components of soil?
mcq.explanation: The main components of soil are mineral particles, organic matter, water, air and living organisms; plastic is not a natural soil component.

mcq.questionText: The vertical section of soil showing different layers from the surface to the parent rock is called the:
mcq.explanation: A soil profile is the vertical arrangement of soil layers (horizons) seen when a pit is dug from the surface down to the parent material.

mcq.questionText: The uppermost soil layer that is dark in colour and rich in humus is known as the:
mcq.explanation: The topsoil (A horizon) is the surface layer that is dark and rich in humus, where most crop roots grow.

mcq.questionText: Which type of soil has the largest particles and drains water very quickly?
mcq.explanation: Sandy soil is made of large particles with wide spaces between them, so water drains through it quickly.

mcq.questionText: Which soil type is considered the best for growing most crops?
mcq.explanation: Loam soil contains a balanced mixture of sand, silt and clay, giving good drainage, aeration and water-holding capacity for most crops.

mcq.questionText: The relative proportion of sand, silt and clay particles in a soil is referred to as soil:
mcq.explanation: Soil texture describes the relative amounts of sand, silt and clay particles in a soil.

mcq.questionText: The way soil particles join together to form clumps or aggregates is called soil:
mcq.explanation: Soil structure refers to the arrangement of individual soil particles into aggregates or clumps.

mcq.questionText: Which property of soil refers to the amount of pore spaces present that hold air and water?
mcq.explanation: Porosity is the proportion of pore spaces in the soil that hold air and water between the particles.

mcq.questionText: A soil with a pH value below 7 is described as:
mcq.explanation: A pH value below 7 indicates an acidic soil, while above 7 is alkaline and exactly 7 is neutral.

mcq.questionText: Which material is commonly added to acidic soil to reduce its acidity?
mcq.explanation: Lime is added to acidic soils to raise the pH and reduce acidity, making the soil more suitable for crops.

mcq.questionText: The partly decomposed organic matter that gives topsoil its dark colour and improves fertility is called:
mcq.explanation: Humus is decomposed organic matter that improves soil fertility, structure and water-holding capacity.

mcq.questionText: A fertile soil is one that:

options.text: Supplies plants with enough nutrients, water and air for growth

mcq.explanation: Soil fertility is the ability of soil to supply crops with adequate nutrients, water and air needed for healthy growth.

fib.questionText: The thin top layer of the earth in which plants grow is called _____.
fib.explanation: Soil is the natural top layer of the earth that supports plant growth.

fib.questionText: The process of breaking down rocks into small particles to form soil is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Weathering breaks rocks into smaller fragments that form the mineral part of soil.

fib.questionText: The dark, decomposed organic matter in the soil is called _____.
fib.explanation: Humus results from the decay of plant and animal remains and improves soil fertility.

fib.questionText: The vertical arrangement of soil layers from the surface to the parent rock is called the soil _____.
fib.explanation: A soil profile shows the different horizons of the soil.

fib.questionText: Each distinct layer seen in a soil profile is known as a soil _____.
fib.explanation: Soil horizons are the separate layers that make up a soil profile.

fib.questionText: The soil type made up of very fine, sticky particles that hold a lot of water is _____ soil.
fib.explanation: Clay soil has tiny particles, holds much water and drains poorly.

fib.questionText: The relative proportion of sand, silt and clay in a soil is called soil _____.
fib.explanation: Soil texture is determined by the proportions of the different sized mineral particles.

fib.questionText: A soil with a pH of exactly 7 is described as _____.
fib.explanation: A pH of 7 is neutral, neither acidic nor alkaline.

fib.questionText: The ability of a soil to hold water for use by plants is called its water-holding _____.
fib.explanation: Water-holding capacity is the amount of water a soil can retain for plant use.

fib.questionText: The substance added to acidic soils to raise their pH is called _____.
fib.explanation: Lime neutralises soil acidity and raises the pH towards neutral.

tf.questionText: Soil is a non-living material that does not contain any organisms.
tf.explanation: Soil contains many living organisms such as earthworms, bacteria and fungi.

tf.questionText: Weathering can be caused by physical, chemical and biological processes.
tf.explanation: Rocks are broken down by physical, chemical and biological weathering.

tf.questionText: Sandy soil holds more water than clay soil.
tf.explanation: Clay soil holds much more water than sandy soil because of its very fine particles.

tf.questionText: Loam soil is generally the best soil for growing most crops.
tf.explanation: Loam combines good drainage, aeration, nutrients and water-holding capacity.

tf.questionText: The topsoil contains more humus than the subsoil.
tf.explanation: The topsoil is richer in organic matter and humus than the subsoil below it.

tf.questionText: A soil with a pH of 9 is acidic.
tf.explanation: A pH of 9 is above 7, so the soil is alkaline, not acidic.

tf.questionText: Air and water are both found in the pore spaces of the soil.
tf.explanation: The pore spaces between soil particles hold both air and water.

tf.questionText: Soil texture refers to how soil particles join together to form aggregates.
tf.explanation: Texture refers to the proportion of particle sizes; the joining into aggregates is soil structure.

tf.questionText: Adding organic matter to soil can improve both its fertility and water-holding capacity.
tf.explanation: Organic matter releases nutrients and improves the soil's ability to retain water.

tf.questionText: Soil is not important for crop production because plants get everything from the air.
tf.explanation: Soil provides anchorage, water, nutrients and air that plants need to grow.

summary.correctAnswer: Soil is the thin top layer of the earth in which plants grow.
summary.explanation: It supports plant life by providing anchorage, water, air and nutrients.

summary.correctAnswer: Soil forms through the weathering of rocks and the addition of organic matter.
summary.explanation: Rock particles mix with decayed plant and animal remains over a long time.

summary.correctAnswer: Soil is made of mineral particles, organic matter, water, air and living organisms.
summary.explanation: These components together support plant growth.

summary.correctAnswer: A soil profile is the vertical section of soil layers from surface to parent rock.
summary.explanation: It is made up of horizons such as topsoil, subsoil and parent material.

summary.correctAnswer: The three main soil types are sandy, clay and loam soil.
summary.explanation: They differ in particle size, drainage and water-holding capacity.

summary.correctAnswer: Sandy soil has large particles, drains quickly and holds little water.
summary.explanation: It is well aerated but low in nutrients and water retention.

summary.correctAnswer: Clay soil has very fine particles, holds much water and drains poorly.
summary.explanation: It becomes sticky when wet and hard when dry.

summary.correctAnswer: Texture is the proportion of particle sizes; structure is how particles form aggregates.
summary.explanation: Both affect drainage, aeration and root growth.

summary.correctAnswer: Soil pH measures how acidic or alkaline the soil is, on a scale of 0 to 14.
summary.explanation: Below 7 is acidic, 7 is neutral and above 7 is alkaline.

summary.correctAnswer: Soil provides anchorage, water, air and nutrients needed for crop growth.
summary.explanation: Healthy fertile soil leads to good yields.

hoq.questionText: A farmer notices that water collects on the surface of his field after rain and takes a long time to drain away, and the soil becomes very hard when dry. Which soil type is he most likely farming, and why?

options.text: Sandy soil, because it drains too quickly
Loam soil, because it has balanced drainage
Clay soil, because its fine particles cause poor drainage and it hardens when dry
Gravel, because it cannot hold any water

hoq.explanation: Clay soil has very fine, closely packed particles that drain slowly, hold water on the surface and harden when dry.

hoq.questionText: A soil test on a farm gives a pH reading of 4.5, and crops are growing poorly. What is the most appropriate action for the farmer to take?

options.text: Add more acidic fertiliser to lower the pH further
Apply lime to raise the pH and reduce acidity
Add sand to change the soil texture

hoq.explanation: A pH of 4.5 is strongly acidic; applying lime raises the pH toward neutral, improving nutrient availability and crop growth.

hoq.questionText: Two fields have the same crop, but the field with regular addition of manure and compost produces higher yields than the one without. Which conclusion best explains this difference?

options.text: Manure and compost increase organic matter, improving soil fertility and water-holding capacity
Manure makes the soil more acidic and less fertile
Compost removes all nutrients from the soil
Organic matter has no effect on crop yield

hoq.explanation: Manure and compost add organic matter that supplies nutrients and improves soil structure and water retention, raising yields.
